ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, there is a smooth, insulated long plank $B$ with a vertical barrier attached to its right end, resting stationary on a smooth horizontal ground. A slider $A$, which can be considered as a point mass, is placed on the long plank. The distance between $A$ and the right barrier of $B$ is $L$, and the distance between $A$ and the left end of $B$ is sufficiently large. Both $A$ and $B$ (including the barrier) have a mass of $m$. The slider $A$ carries a charge of $+q$. Initially, both $A$ and $B$ are at rest. If a uniform electric field of magnitude $E$ and direction horizontally to the right is applied in this space, $A$ will start moving to the right due to the electric force and will collide elastically with $B$. The collision between $A$ and $B$ occurs over an extremely short time interval, and there is no charge transfer during the collision. Find:

1. After the first collision between $A$ and $B$, what is the speed of $B$?
2. What is the time elapsed from the start of motion at $A$ until the second collision between $A$ and $B$?
3. What is the distance traveled by the long plank $B$ from the $n$-th collision to the $(n+1)$-th collision between $A$ and $B$?

Only the charged slider A is subject to the electric field force qE, so the acceleration of A between two collisions is a=qE/m; the wooden board B is not subject to horizontal external force outside collisions and remains at uniform speed. Before the first collision, B is at rest, and A starts from rest and travels L relative to the stop plate, so L=(1/2)at_1^2, therefore t_1=sqrt(2L/a), and the velocity of A before collision is v_1=at_1=sqrt(2aL)=sqrt(2qEL/m). A and B of equal mass undergo a one-dimensional elastic collision, and the collision time is extremely short, so the impulse of the electric field can be ignored; therefore the velocities are exchanged. After the first collision, the velocity of B is v_1=sqrt(2qEL/m), and the velocity of A is 0. After the first collision, A starts from velocity 0 and continues to accelerate to the right, and B and the stop plate move uniformly to the right with velocity v_1. Let the time from the first collision to the second collision be tau, then the relative displacement is again zero: 0=(-v_1)tau+(1/2)a tau^2, and the nonzero solution is tau=2v_1/a. Therefore the total time from the start to the second collision is t_1+tau=v_1/a+2v_1/a=3v_1/a=3sqrt(2mL/(qE)). Further, by induction, after the nth collision, the velocity of B is n v_1, and the velocity of A is (n-1)v_1. The relative initial velocity between two collisions is always -v_1, and the relative acceleration is a, so the interval is still tau=2v_1/a. Between the nth and the (n+1)th collisions, B moves uniformly, and the displacement s_n=(n v_1)tau=n v_1(2v_1/a)=2n v_1^2/a=2n(2aL)/a=4nL.

First read the figure as: block A sits on the smooth plank B, to the left of a vertical barrier fixed at B’s right end, and the horizontal gap from A to the barrier is L. From the text take that A and B have equal mass m, only A has charge +q, the uniform electric field points right, the plank and ground are smooth, and the collisions with the barrier are elastic and instantaneous. Before the first collision, A starts from rest and travels distance L relative to the stationary barrier, so use L=1/2 at_1^2 and v_1=at_1 to get v_1=sqrt(2qEL/m). For an elastic one-dimensional collision of equal masses, velocities exchange, so after the first collision B’s speed is v_1. Then after the first collision A has speed 0 and B/barrier has speed v_1; solve catch-up equation 1/2 a tau^2=v_1 tau to get tau=2v_1/a, and total time to the second collision is t_1+tau=3sqrt(2mL/qE). For later collisions, prove by induction that after the n-th collision B has speed nv_1 and A has speed (n-1)v_1. method.method_draft: Energy plus collision-map method. First read the drawing: A is a small slider on a horizontal plank B, the vertical wall fixed on B is to A’s right, and the initial horizontal separation is L. From the text take that A alone is charged and experiences the rightward electric force qE; the surfaces are smooth, and A and B have equal mass m. For the first approach, avoid solving time first: the electric field does work qEL on A before it reaches the initially stationary wall, so 1/2 mv_0^2=qEL and v_0=sqrt(2qEL/m). During the instantaneous elastic collision, neglect electric impulse and use conservation of momentum plus kinetic energy for two equal masses to show the velocities exchange, giving B speed v_0 after the first collision. Then construct a discrete post-collision map: at each collision the pre-collision velocities exchange, while between collisions only A gains speed from the field. After the n-th collision assume B has speed nv_0 and A has speed (n-1)v_0. A must gain exactly 2v_0 in speed before the next collision because it starts one v_0 slower than the barrier and must close the gap after falling behind; equivalently solve relative motion to get Delta t=2v_0/a, where a=qE/m. Therefore total time to the second collision is the initial time v_0/a plus 2v_0/a, and the plank displacement during the n-th interval is nv_0·2v_0/a=4nL.

raw_record.original_question:
As shown in the figure, there is a smooth, insulated long plank $B$ with a vertical barrier attached to its right end, resting stationary on a smooth horizontal ground. A slider $A$, which can be considered as a point mass, is placed on the long plank. The distance between $A$ and the right barrier of $B$ is $L$, and the distance between $A$ and the left end of $B$ is sufficiently large. Both $A$ and $B$ (including the barrier) have a mass of $m$. The slider $A$ carries a charge of $+q$. Initially, both $A$ and $B$ are at rest. If a uniform electric field of magnitude $E$ and direction horizontally to the right is applied in this space, $A$ will start moving to the right due to the electric force and will collide elastically with $B$. The collision between $A$ and $B$ occurs over an extremely short time interval, and there is no charge transfer during the collision. Find:

1. After the first collision between $A$ and $B$, what is the speed of $B$?
2. What is the time elapsed from the start of motion at $A$ until the second collision between $A$ and $B$?
3. What is the distance traveled by the long plank $B$ from the $n$-th collision to the $(n+1)$-th collision between $A$ and $B$?
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, slider A is placed on the upper surface of the long wooden board B, and a vertical stop plate is fixed at the right end of B; A is located on the left side of the stop plate, the horizontal distance from A to the right-end stop plate is marked as L, and the wooden board is on the horizontal ground. Reasoning: Take horizontally to the right as positive. Only the charged slider A is subject to the electric field force qE, so the acceleration of A between two collisions is a=qE/m; the wooden board B is not subject to horizontal external force outside collisions and remains at uniform speed. Before the first collision, B is at rest, and A starts from rest and travels L relative to the stop plate, so L=(1/2)at_1^2, therefore t_1=sqrt(2L/a), and the velocity of A before collision is v_1=at_1=sqrt(2aL)=sqrt(2qEL/m). A and B of equal mass undergo a one-dimensional elastic collision, and the collision time is extremely short, so the impulse of the electric field can be ignored; therefore the velocities are exchanged. After the first collision, the velocity of B is v_1=sqrt(2qEL/m), and the velocity of A is 0. After the first collision, A starts from velocity 0 and continues to accelerate to the right, and B and the stop plate move uniformly to the right with velocity v_1. Let the time from the first collision to the second collision be tau, then the relative displacement is again zero: 0=(-v_1)tau+(1/2)a tau^2, and the nonzero solution is tau=2v_1/a. Therefore the total time from the start to the second collision is t_1+tau=v_1/a+2v_1/a=3v_1/a=3sqrt(2mL/(qE)). Further, by induction, after the nth collision, the velocity of B is n v_1, and the velocity of A is (n-1)v_1. The relative initial velocity between two collisions is always -v_1, and the relative acceleration is a, so the interval is still tau=2v_1/a. Between the nth and the (n+1)th collisions, B moves uniformly, and the displacement s_n=(n v_1)tau=n v_1(2v_1/a)=2n v_1^2/a=2n(2aL)/a=4nL.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, slider A is placed on the upper surface of the long wooden board B, and a vertical stop plate is fixed at the right end of B; A is located on the left side of the stop plate, the horizontal distance from A to the right-end stop plate is marked as L, and the wooden board is on the horizontal ground. Reasoning: Take horizontally to the right as positive. Only the charged slider A is subject to the electric field force qE, so the acceleration of A between two collisions is a=qE/m; the wooden board B is not subject to horizontal external force outside collisions and remains at uniform speed. Before the first collision, B is at rest, and A starts from rest and travels L relative to the stop plate, so L=(1/2)at_1^2, therefore t_1=sqrt(2L/a), and the velocity of A before collision is v_1=at_1=sqrt(2aL)=sqrt(2qEL/m). A and B of equal mass undergo a one-dimensional elastic collision, and the collision time is extremely short, so the impulse of the electric field can be ignored; therefore the velocities are exchanged. After the first collision, the velocity of B is v_1=sqrt(2qEL/m), and the velocity of A is 0. After the first collision, A starts from velocity 0 and continues to accelerate to the right, and B and the stop plate move uniformly to the right with velocity v_1. Let the time from the first collision to the second collision be tau, then the relative displacement is again zero: 0=(-v_1)tau+(1/2)a tau^2, and the nonzero solution is tau=2v_1/a. Therefore the total time from the start to the second collision is t_1+tau=v_1/a+2v_1/a=3v_1/a=3sqrt(2mL/(qE)). Further, by induction, after the nth collision, the velocity of B is n v_1, and the velocity of A is (n-1)v_1. The relative initial velocity between two collisions is always -v_1, and the relative acceleration is a, so the interval is still tau=2v_1/a. Between the nth and the (n+1)th collisions, B moves uniformly, and the displacement s_n=(n v_1)tau=n v_1(2v_1/a)=2n v_1^2/a=2n(2aL)/a=4nL.
